teaching_point: Steroid telangiectasia on facial skin after prolonged steroid use — face and eyelids are the highest-risk sites; use mild potency short-term or a TCI; periocular steroid also risks glaucoma/cataract.

teaching_point: Easy bruising/purpura on steroid-thinned forearm skin (dermal collagen loss).

teaching_point: Steroid-induced rosacea — facial use of potent TCS; rebound flare when stopped. Topical steroids are contraindicated in rosacea.

attribution: Image: DermNet — Steroid rosacea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/steroid-rosacea

teaching_point: Perioral dermatitis from a steroid nebuliser mask — steroid exposure from any route (cream, inhaler/nebuliser spacer mask) provokes it; stop steroid (expect rebound), consider topical metronidazole/azelaic or oral tetracycline (>12 y).
dermnet_caption: Perioral dermatitis due to the use of a steroid nebuliser mask
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Tinea incognita — fungal infection modified by steroid (less scale, spreading, pustules). Untreated fungal infection is a steroid contraindication; scrape before steroids if annular/asymmetric.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Tinea incognita - limb (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tinea-incognito

teaching_point: Localised pustular psoriasis — potent steroids on extensive psoriasis can provoke unstable/pustular rebound (BNF caution); also why oral steroids are avoided in psoriasis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Localised pustular psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/topical-steroid

teaching_point: Positive patch test to budesonide — corticosteroid contact allergy; suspect when eczema worsens or fails to settle on TCS. Refer for patch testing.

teaching_point: Eyelid redness and swelling after stopping prolonged potent facial steroid — topical steroid withdrawal reaction (MHRA DSU Sept 2021).
dermnet_caption: Redness and swelling of the lids - steroid withdrawal after prolonged potent steroid use on the face.

teaching_point: "Red sleeve" sign — confluent forearm erythema with sharp cut-off at the wrist (palms spared) after abrupt cessation of long-term potent TCS (MHRA 2021).
dermnet_caption: Redness and swelling of the forearm after abrupt discontinuation of prolonged potent topical steroid use. Palms are not affected (red sleeve sign).

teaching_point: Fingertip unit — ointment from a 5 mm nozzle, distal crease to tip of an ADULT index finger (≈0.5 g) covers two adult palms.

teaching_point: Topical steroids in different vehicles (ointment, cream, lotion, scalp application, foam) — the same molecule changes effective potency with vehicle/occlusion.

teaching_point: Emollients from light to greasy — "the right one is the one the patient will use"; children need 250–500 g/week. Avoid aqueous cream as leave-on.

teaching_point: Natal cleft/buttock psoriasis before calcipotriol. Note: calcipotriol can irritate flexures — calcitriol is better tolerated there.

teaching_point: Same patient after 6 weeks of calcipotriol ointment — anti-proliferative/pro-differentiating vitamin D analogue response.

teaching_point: Coal tar preparation on the hands — messy, staining, odour; use as steroid-sparing for chronic plaque/scalp psoriasis.

teaching_point: Hand-and-foot PUVA unit — localised (soak/topical psoralen) PUVA for palmoplantar psoriasis, pustulosis or chronic hand eczema; hospital-delivered. Oral PUVA needs UVA-blocking eye protection for ~24 h; cumulative-dose SCC risk.

teaching_point: Minimal erythema dose (MED) testing to set the starting NB-UVB (311–313 nm) dose — first-line phototherapy for psoriasis/eczema in UK services.
dermnet_caption: MED testing to determine initial dose of UVB

teaching_point: Sunburn on isotretinoin — photosensitivity and skin fragility; counsel SPF 30+ / UVA, avoid sunbeds; no waxing/laser/dermabrasion during and for 6 months after.

teaching_point: Impetigo during isotretinoin — dry, cracked skin and S. aureus colonisation (cheilitis/nasal vestibule); treat per NICE NG153.

teaching_point: Retinoid dermatitis (dryness/peeling) from a topical retinoid — start alternate nights, pea-sized amount, moisturiser; topical retinoids are avoided in pregnancy.

teaching_point: Acitretin nail fragility/paronychia — common mucocutaneous effect. Acitretin needs pregnancy prevention for 3 YEARS after stopping and no alcohol (etretinate formation).

teaching_point: Diffuse hair shedding on acitretin — dose-related telogen effluvium, usually reversible after stopping.

teaching_point: Modified Ferriman–Gallwey visual scale — 9 androgen-sensitive sites scored 0–4 (max 36); ≥8 usually defines hirsutism in white/black women (lower cut-offs in East Asian women). Case score of 2 at jaw/sideburns = localised/mild.

teaching_point: Facial terminal hair on chin and upper lip — measure impact (distress) not just score: "treat patients, not labs/scores".

teaching_point: Jawline/side-of-chin terminal hair.

teaching_point: Folliculitis after hair removal — common complication of shaving/waxing/epilation; pseudofolliculitis in curly hair; laser in darker skin needs Nd:YAG and an experienced operator.
